keyVerseText: And Mattithiah, one of the Levites, who was the firstborn of Shallum the Korahite, had the set office over the things that were made in the pans. set: or, trust in: or, on flat plates, or, slices
rootMeaning: The root of חָבֵת (châbêth) is connected to an unused root likely meaning 'to cook,' which is supported by its relation to מַחֲבַת (machăbath), a term for a baking pan or griddle. This etymology highlights the word's literal association with the preparation of food by cooking on a flat surface, adding a tangible sense of the physical process involved rather than simply referring to the food product itself. Thus, חָבֵת conveys not just the idea of a baked item, but specifically something made by cooking on a pan or griddle, emphasizing the method and setting of its preparation.
usageInScripture: The word חָבֵת appears only once in Scripture, specifically in 1 Chronicles 9:31, where it is translated as 'in the pans.' This singular occurrence limits the range of its usage but provides a clear context related to food preparation, particularly flat cakes or bread wafers made on pans. The consistency in translation underscores its meaning as a term closely tied to the physical implements and process of baking or frying, rather than a broader or metaphorical usage.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding חָבֵת enriches our appreciation of the tangible and everyday aspects of biblical life, reminding us that God’s Word encompasses not only grand spiritual truths but also the ordinary, faithful service in daily tasks. The specificity of this term highlights the ordered and intentional nature of Levitical duties, reflecting how God’s people were called to serve Him in both sacred and practical ways. This attention to detail in Scripture assures believers that God values faithful stewardship in all areas, including the preparation of food, which sustains life. Moreover, the connection to cooking on a pan points to the provision and care God extends to His people, foreshadowing the spiritual nourishment found in Christ, the Bread of Life.
keyVerseReflection: In 1 Chronicles 9:31, the phrase 'had the set office over the things that were made in the pans' points to a specific Levitical responsibility involving the preparation of food items like flat cakes or bread wafers. The use of חָבֵת here emphasizes the practical service entrusted to Mattithiah, highlighting the sacredness even in mundane tasks. This word draws attention to the care and order God requires in worship and community life, showing that serving Him includes diligence in all appointed roles, no matter how ordinary they may seem.
